This 100% critically rated TV show follows a small group of individuals who suddenly develop varying superhuman talents, like invisibility, time manipulation, and telekinesis. With superhero fatigue becoming a real issue for audiences, Supacell brings something entirely new to the table and reminds fans why the genre is so rich.

Supacell tackles some of the tried-and-true ethical questions about superpowers, like using them for personal gain and carrying out an immediate view of justice. blocks.c: Dan Stevens in Legion staring ahead.

blocks.x: Legion is a psychedelic, trippy, and fantastical foray into the superhero genre. Dan Stevens plays the role of David Haller, a man who has been diagnosed as a person with schizophrenia because of symptoms like hearing voices. David learns that his psychic abilities are only the tip of the iceberg, and he has infinitely more power than he had ever assumed.

Legion is based in the X-Men universe and does credit to the comic book mythos of its origin. David is a powerful mutant who has never been taught how to control his abilities. As he comes to terms with the newfound might he can wield, he must face several crises of conscience and decide whether he is going to be a hero or a villain. Legion taps into the core idea of the X-Men comics about prejudice and segregation for people groups deemed as "other." It is an artistic and phenomenally well done series, and many superhero TV shows that have come after owe it something.

blocks.x: A TV series that spawned from the larger MCU but presented something entirely unexpected to audiences was WandaVision. The story follows the character Wanda Maximoff, an extremely powerful being known as the Scarlet Witch. Elizabeth Olsen originated the role in the MCU, and it is perfection to watch her solidify her legacy in the role on the small screen. It launched two sequel series with the latest, Vision Quest, coming to streaming this October.

WandaVision did not begin like any other Marvel TV show. In fact, it took several episodes for it to feel like anything the MCU had released so far. It was a bold and daring creative choice, but one that ultimately paid off, as the series is as close to perfection as any superhero TV show has come yet. Pain, loss, love, suffering — all of these powerful emotions combine with limitless power in the person of Wanda Maximoff. With her ability to manipulate reality, the central question becomes: if you had the power to build your version of a perfect life, would it be real? WandaVision moves through eras of classic TV shows, examining how idealistic family life was defined in each era. It is an undisputed masterpiece and proves that comic book fans have room in their hearts for creative journeys that take unique approaches to the storytelling process.

blocks.c: Mark flying through the air in Invincible Season 4

blocks.x: A coming-of-age story about a young person adapting to life with superpowers is a classic trope within the milieu, but that is only where Invincible starts. The series soon begins to reveal itself as something much more profound and introspective as layer after layer slowly sheds. Since the very beginning, audiences and critics alike have raved about this absolute triumph, and with Season 5 and a possible Season 6 around the corner, Invincible is still gaining momentum.

Animation has been a staple in the superhero genre and for very good reason. It is a harkening back to the original art form that made the stories memorable: comic books. With its stunning graphics and bold, vibrant colors, Invincible is as visually gripping as it is emotionally impactful. Over such a prestigious run, there have been many opportunities to explore compelling topics, and Invincible does it better than most. It is a fan and critic darling for many reasons and is more than worthy of a spot on this list.

blocks.c: John Cena as Peacemaker in 'Peacemaker' flexing his muscles

blocks.x: The DCU can do dark really well, and the hit series Peacemaker proves they can also do dark comedy to perfection. A spin-off TV series from the DCU, Peacemaker stars John Cena in his role as the titular superhero, or his mundane alter ego, Christopher Smith. The TV show picks up where James Gunn's The Suicide Squad left off and follows the red-and-blue-clad protagonist as he works as a hired gun for the government.

Peacemaker is a pièce de résistance that combines the best of the past and the present. It is a must-watch for fans of classic '80s and '90s superhero projects and delivers nostalgia in an energetic adrenaline rush with a healthy dose of Americana thrown in. It is snarky, smart, and everything adult fans of the genre would want in a show that feels like an open love-letter to the genre. Peacemaker ticks all the boxes for examining the highs, lows, and ironic idiosyncrasies of trying to be perfect in an imperfect world. It blends humor with poignant moments and delivers on all fronts. Peacemaker has a fantastic ensemble cast and is one of the best superhero TV shows of any era.

blocks.c: Tom Hiddleston as President Loki wearing a campaign button and smiling in Loki TV series

blocks.x: Having catapulted to the forefront of fans’ minds in the MCU, Tom Hiddleston's God of Mischief got his own TV series in 2021, Loki. The mercurial menace struck again, but this time with an entirely original plotline to follow. In the series, Loki is pressed into service to help a time management company called the Time Variance Authority, or TVA. The TVA exists to protect what they call the “sacred timeline,” which involves tackling any variant branches or people that depart from the main history.

Loki is a kaleidoscopic explosion of talent and genres. It is part superhero, part sci-fi, and part fantasy. The cast is one of the best assembled and includes Owen Wilson, Wunmi Mosaku, Sophia Di Martino, Gugu Mbatha-Raw, and Ke Huy Quan. The premise of the series is a brilliant way to tell a unique story outside of the main MCU. It gives viewers a captivating and cerebral series to enjoy, without interfering with any of the events that take place in the movie series. Loki tackles multiverses and time travel better than scores of other TV shows that have come before or since. It has wit and charm, and offers something for everyone to enjoy. The mise en scène ranges from retro to futuristic, and the whole series is visually stunning. Loki is emotionally compelling at times and mixes humor in without being kitschy or overdone. Loki is an all around stunner and tells a fantastic story that anyone from any timeline can appreciate.

The cast is abundantly talented, and the storylines are anchored by deep, relational connections that make the series feel candid. 5
'Legion' (2017–2019)

Image via FX

Legion is a psychedelic, trippy, and fantastical foray into the superhero genre. Dan Stevens plays the role of David Haller, a man who has been diagnosed as a person with schizophrenia because of symptoms like hearing voices. David learns that his psychic abilities are only the tip of the iceberg, and he has infinitely more power than he had ever assumed.

Legion is based in the X-Men universe and does credit to the comic book mythos of its origin. David is a powerful mutant who has never been taught how to control his abilities. As he comes to terms with the newfound might he can wield, he must face several crises of conscience and decide whether he is going to be a hero or a villain. Legion taps into the core idea of the X-Men comics about prejudice and segregation for people groups deemed as "other." It is an artistic and phenomenally well done series, and many superhero TV shows that have come after owe it something.

4

A TV series that spawned from the larger MCU but presented something entirely unexpected to audiences was WandaVision. The story follows the character Wanda Maximoff, an extremely powerful being known as the Scarlet Witch. Elizabeth Olsen originated the role in the MCU, and it is perfection to watch her solidify her legacy in the role on the small screen. It launched two sequel series with the latest, Vision Quest, coming to streaming this October.

WandaVision did not begin like any other Marvel TV show. In fact, it took several episodes for it to feel like anything the MCU had released so far. It was a bold and daring creative choice, but one that ultimately paid off, as the series is as close to perfection as any superhero TV show has come yet. Pain, loss, love, suffering — all of these powerful emotions combine with limitless power in the person of Wanda Maximoff. With her ability to manipulate reality, the central question becomes: if you had the power to build your version of a perfect life, would it be real? WandaVision moves through eras of classic TV shows, examining how idealistic family life was defined in each era. It is an undisputed masterpiece and proves that comic book fans have room in their hearts for creative journeys that take unique approaches to the storytelling process.

3
'Invincible' (2021–Present)

Image via Prime Video

A coming-of-age story about a young person adapting to life with superpowers is a classic trope within the milieu, but that is only where Invincible starts. The series soon begins to reveal itself as something much more profound and introspective as layer after layer slowly sheds. Since the very beginning, audiences and critics alike have raved about this absolute triumph, and with Season 5 and a possible Season 6 around the corner, Invincible is still gaining momentum.

Animation has been a staple in the superhero genre and for very good reason. It is a harkening back to the original art form that made the stories memorable: comic books. With its stunning graphics and bold, vibrant colors, Invincible is as visually gripping as it is emotionally impactful. Over such a prestigious run, there have been many opportunities to explore compelling topics, and Invincible does it better than most. It is a fan and critic darling for many reasons and is more than worthy of a spot on this list.

2
'Peacemaker' (2022–2025)

Image via HBO Max

The DCU can do dark really well, and the hit series Peacemaker proves they can also do dark comedy to perfection. A spin-off TV series from the DCU, Peacemaker stars John Cena in his role as the titular superhero, or his mundane alter ego, Christopher Smith. The TV show picks up where James Gunn's The Suicide Squad left off and follows the red-and-blue-clad protagonist as he works as a hired gun for the government.

Peacemaker is a pièce de résistance that combines the best of the past and the present. It is a must-watch for fans of classic '80s and '90s superhero projects and delivers nostalgia in an energetic adrenaline rush with a healthy dose of Americana thrown in. It is snarky, smart, and everything adult fans of the genre would want in a show that feels like an open love-letter to the genre. Peacemaker ticks all the boxes for examining the highs, lows, and ironic idiosyncrasies of trying to be perfect in an imperfect world. It blends humor with poignant moments and delivers on all fronts. Peacemaker has a fantastic ensemble cast and is one of the best superhero TV shows of any era.

1
'Loki' (2021–2023)

Image via Disney+

Having catapulted to the forefront of fans’ minds in the MCU, Tom Hiddleston's God of Mischief got his own TV series in 2021, Loki. The mercurial menace struck again, but this time with an entirely original plotline to follow. In the series, Loki is pressed into service to help a time management company called the Time Variance Authority, or TVA. The TVA exists to protect what they call the “sacred timeline,” which involves tackling any variant branches or people that depart from the main history.

Loki is a kaleidoscopic explosion of talent and genres. It is part superhero, part sci-fi, and part fantasy. The cast is one of the best assembled and includes Owen Wilson, Wunmi Mosaku, Sophia Di Martino, Gugu Mbatha-Raw, and Ke Huy Quan. The premise of the series is a brilliant way to tell a unique story outside of the main MCU. It gives viewers a captivating and cerebral series to enjoy, without interfering with any of the events that take place in the movie series. Loki tackles multiverses and time travel better than scores of other TV shows that have come before or since. It has wit and charm, and offers something for everyone to enjoy. The mise en scène ranges from retro to futuristic, and the whole series is visually stunning. Loki is emotionally compelling at times and mixes humor in without being kitschy or overdone. Loki is an all around stunner and tells a fantastic story that anyone from any timeline can appreciate.
